main_text.p: vis ex notis, indiciisque utplurimùm sumpta.

II. Primum fuerit ex parte materia-rum, sententiarumque, quas passim author insperfit, quæque Paulum primâ fronte referunt. Neque de generali illo consensu, & quoad doctrinæ substantiam, qualis inter omnes scriptores sacros, sed planè singulari, & quoad doctrinæ similem modum. Ut accidit, scriptorem eundem reponere subinde eadem, & suis se prodere notis. Quod Paulo cumprimis familiare, & authorem arguit pagina quæque suum. Oecumenius, αὐτῷ τυγχάνειν ἐπι-στολὴν[?], ἡ ἀνάγνωσις αὐτὴ διδάσκει. Nec quæremus nodum in scirpo, neque animus est anxius & scrupulosius singula ἐξουχίζειν[?], & congruentiæ umbras omnes sectari. Sat fuerit, ex indicijs quibusdam magè perspicuis, dignoscere ὅπῃ τῆ πατρὸς τὸ παιδίον[?].

III. Quod licet vel ex fronte perspicere, & observari in limine possunt coacervata illa de Christo elogia Hebr.1.verf.2,3. In quibus sigillatim animadvertere est, & phrasim Paulinam, & genium, & ordinem eundem omninò, quem

page.notes: Page number read as 373 (the top-right numeral is partly blurred). Running head reads "ad Hebraeos", the æ possibly printed as ae. Greek words in the Oecumenius quotation and ἐξουχίζειν, ὅπῃ τῆ πατρὸς are doubtful at several letters and marked [?]; the hyphenated "ἐπι-στολὴν" is partly obscured. The first word "sumpta" is partly damaged at the left edge, and the initial letter may be an f-like long s; read as sumpta.
